construct: PHEX loss of function increases FGF23 activity. Excess FGF23 reduces proximal-tubular phosphate reabsorption by promoting internalization of sodium-phosphate cotransporters and also lowers calcitriol synthesis, producing chronic phosphate wasting and defective bone mineralization.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: PHEX-related hypophosphatemic rickets with dental disease and renal phosphate wasting is mediated by excess FGF23, which reduces proximal-tubular phosphate reabsorption by internalizing sodium-phosphate cotransporters.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: PTH excess and SLC34A3 loss are genuine phosphaturic alternatives, but the explicit PHEX diagnosis makes FGF23 excess the operative signal. Vitamin-D-receptor disease and Fanconi syndrome produce different biochemical or generalized proximal-tubular patterns.
